blocks.content: Article 32 was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the very heart and soul of the Constitution.

rows: Empowers Citizens to approach SC directly; called 'Heart & Soul' of Constitution
Certified solely by Speaker of Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend
Quasi-judicial body constituted by the President every 5 years for tax distribution
Imposed when constitutional machinery fails in a state; requires Parliamentary approval
Outlines Parliament's constituent power to amend provisions subject to Basic Structure doctrine

items: Article 324 governs the Election Commission; frequently tested in match-the-following and direct factual questions.
Article 51A defines Fundamental Duties, introduced via the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on Swaran Singh Committee recommendations.
Article 112 refers to the Annual Financial Statement; the word 'Budget' is not explicitly used in the Constitution.
Article 368 governs Constitutional amendments, which require special majority and cannot trigger a joint sitting of Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 14 to 18 guarantee the Right to Equality, prohibiting discrimination and abolishing untouchability and titles.
Article 21 protects Right to Life and Personal Liberty, serving as the foundation for modern rights like privacy and education.
Article 32 confers the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights through constitutional writs.
Article 110 strictly defines Money Bills, giving exclusive legislative power over financial matters to the Lok Sabha.
Articles 352, 356, and 360 deal with Emergency Provisions: National Emergency, President's Rule, and Financial Emergency.
